Hemoperfusion-hemodialysis ineffective for paraquat removal in life-threatening poisoning? We report on a patient treated with hemoperfusion-hemodialysis (HP-HD) for severe paraquat poisoning. This procedure was adopted since the combination of adsorption and dialysis may improve overall drug removal. On admission blood paraquat was 15.8 micrograms/ml. He received conventional treatment and combined HP-HD which started within 3 hours after ingestion of the chemical and lasted 5 hours. Blood samples were obtained during and after HP-HD. The samples during HP-HD were taken before the charcoal column, between the charcoal column and the artificial kidney and after the artificial kidney.
